_comment: filter x opacity ORDER on one element. Spec (filter-effects-1 §2 + CSS painting order): the filter applies to the element as a group FIRST, and the element's opacity then applies to the FILTERED result at composite time — filter-then-fade, never fade-then-filter. For the nonlinear invert() the two orders give different pixels against a known backdrop, so the composite exposes the order. Structure: parent 200x80 solid #ffffff backdrop, child inset 6px (188x68 = 12784 px vs 3216 px white ring — child dominates). invert(a) per filter-effects-1 §8.5: c' = c*(1-a) + (255-c)*a. ARITHMETIC — OFS_InvertOpaque: invert(1) on #ff0000 -> (0,255,255), opaque: fill (0,255,255). OFS_InvertHalfOpacity: spec order = invert first -> (0,255,255), THEN opacity 0.5 composites over white: 0.5*(0,255,255)+0.5*(255,255,255) = (127.5,255,255) -> (128,255,255)+-1. The fade-then-filter wrong order — inverting the already-backdrop-blended colour — gives invert(0.5*(255,0,0)+0.5*white) = invert(255,127.5,127.5) = (0,127.5,127.5) -> (0,128,128): 128 apart in R, unmissable. Dropping the filter gives (255,128,128); dropping the opacity gives (0,255,255); every failure mode is >=127 from the spec value in some channel. OFS_InvertHalfAmount: invert(0.5) maps EVERY channel to 0.5c+0.5(255-c) = 127.5 -> (128,128,128) regardless of input — an amount-vs-opacity confusion probe (a runtime treating invert's amount as post-filter alpha renders (128,255,255) here instead); grey fill sits on the label-AA axis so box is deliberately unasserted. OFS_NoFilter_Op50_Control: 0.5*(255,0,0)+0.5*white = (255,127.5,127.5) -> (255,128,128) — what a filter-dropping runtime renders for OFS_InvertHalfOpacity. No predicted red: the 2026-08-28 sepia translucency fix (.plusLighter composite) covered filter x alpha on iOS for sepia; this fixture extends the class to invert, where no coverage exists.
